I need to understand the available skills and requirements.

I need to understand listOverdueIssues and project stats overdue counting. I also need to review the organization service, mappers, migrations, and tests that encode old behavior.

I need to update visible tests that encode the old UTC and instant behavior. Date tests likely fail due to instant-based overdue and digest window logic. Activity grouping may still pass if timestamps align with the default UTC timezone. I also need to add a timeZone column to the schema.

The timeZone field belongs inside organization settings. Both the update repository and service accept it there, and every read returns it. Existing and new workspaces default to UTC. The schema accepts timeZone with a default of UTC and rejects unknown zones. The update path must reject invalid zones with a RangeError and leave existing data unchanged.

I am carefully analyzing the calendar-day semantics for this substantial change.

OrganizationSettings will gain a `timeZone` field defaulting to UTC. It will be stored with other settings and validated via Zod, rejecting unknown zones. A new `localDate` helper in `src/lib/date.ts` will derive the calendar date from an ISO timestamp for a given timezone.

`startOfLocalDay` will return the UTC instant at which the local calendar day begins. `isOverdue` will check if the due date's calendar day has already ended in the workspace timezone. An item is not overdue on its own due day.

The old instant-based logic is being replaced by a calendar-day comparison. `isOverdue` now returns true only when the due date's local calendar day has already ended relative to the reference. A task due at 23:00 UTC on March 15th is overdue on March 16th even if the current instant is still in the morning.

A Tokyo example confirms the rule: a task due at 15:00 UTC on March 15th is not overdue until the next day at 15:00 UTC, when it becomes March 17 in Tokyo. The reference timestamp exactly at local midnight of the following day counts as overdue.

`digestWindow` will return the most recent local hour:00 at or before the reference time. It treats today as the current calendar day if that hour has already passed; otherwise it uses yesterday.

The digest window starts at the same local hour on the previous calendar day, so it can span 23 or 25 hours across a DST change. It throws RangeError for hours outside 0–23.

The implementation will extract local date parts in the workspace timezone. If the current local hour is greater than or equal to the digest hour, the window ends today at that hour; otherwise it ends yesterday at that hour.

A DST edge case surfaced: during spring-forward transitions, the previous calendar day at the same local hour may not exist, and during fall-back it may occur twice. A robust helper is needed to convert local year-month-day-hour-minute-second values in a timezone into a UTC instant.

A naive `Date.UTC` guess plus timezone offset was rejected as unsafe. The chosen approach is an iterative refinement: start with a UTC guess, read its local parts in the target timezone, and rebuild the timestamp from those parts until convergence.

The iterative helper will converge by repeatedly adjusting the UTC timestamp until the local parts match the desired values. This naturally handles DST edge cases: during spring-forward transitions, the algorithm lands on the next valid instant; during fall-back, it resolves the ambiguous time. The digest window must still span 23 or 25 hours across these changes.

The 2026 spring-forward transition is March 8 and the fall-back is November 1. The spec does not explicitly handle invalid hours on DST days, only that the window spans 23 or 25 hours. On a spring-forward day the previous calendar day at the same local hour is 23 hours later because clocks jump forward by one hour.

`startOfLocalDay` will return the UTC instant at which the local calendar day containing the reference began, equivalent to local midnight of that local date. `localDate` will return a YYYY-MM-DD string. The implementation will use `Intl.DateTimeFormat.formatToParts` to extract local date parts and let `RangeError` from invalid timezones propagate.

The overdue sweep logic must be updated to compare against `startOfLocalDay(now, timeZone)` instead of the current instant. Any task due at or after local midnight on its calendar day is not yet overdue.

I am weighing two ways to apply the per-organization timezone cutoff: either compute it in the job and pass it to `listOverdueIssues`, or let that function look up the workspace timezone itself. The manifest signature currently takes a single `now` timestamp, but the task does not require changing that interface.
